researchNotes.intro: A different object. A different scene. We look for the structure and relationships that hold through change.

notes.title: Start with the object
notes.description: Understand actions relative to the object, rather than memorize a trajectory in world coordinates.

notes.title: Find geometric constraints
notes.description: Extract contact, spatial structure and interaction relationships from a few demonstrations.

notes.title: Carry the understanding forward
notes.description: Transfer reusable manipulation knowledge to new objects, scenes and robots.

experience.statementBody: The next step in robotics is more than memorizing more actions. It is understanding the structure behind them. Starting with the object, we look for transferable manipulation knowledge in a few demonstrations.

Together.
experience.invitationBody: We welcome researchers, engineers, robot makers and application partners to help bring transferable intelligence into a wider world.
experience.footerBelief: Understand structure. Connect it to action. Teach robots to generalize.
experience.aboutIntro: Start with the object. Build for a world that keeps changing.
experience.teamInvitation: Curious about robotics and the real world? We would love to explore with you.
experience.discussTask: What would you like your robot to learn?
solutionDetails: Explore skill reuse across robot embodiments through object geometry, contact relationships and manipulation constraints, reducing reliance on trajectories tied to a single robot.
Use spatial structure and interaction relationships in demonstrations to explore skill transfer across layouts and objects, connecting collected data to reusable manipulation knowledge.
Discuss how to reduce repeated data collection and tuning for manipulation tasks with changing objects, positions and environments, keeping validation close to the actual task.
experience.collaborationTitle: Understand the task. Explore the path forward.

collaborationSteps.title: Define the task
collaborationSteps.description: Discuss manipulation goals, object variations, environment and robot embodiment to define what needs to be validated.

collaborationSteps.title: Discuss demonstrations
collaborationSteps.description: Consider available demonstrations, object structure and the key interaction relationships involved in the task.

collaborationSteps.title: Explore transfer
collaborationSteps.description: Discuss validation across new objects, layouts or embodiments, and the next steps for collaboration.

about.title: About Xianova
about.company: Xianova Robotics focuses on zero-shot generalization for robot manipulation. We propose the object-centric ORGA architecture so robots understand object structure, spatial constraints, and interaction from few demonstrations — instead of memorizing motion trajectories — and extrapolate across novel objects, scenes, and embodiments.

technology.metaDesc: ORGA — object-centric representation for generalization: object-centric features → geometric constraint extraction → zero-shot transfer.
technology.heroDesc: Object-centric extraction of transferable geometric constraints and spatial structure for zero-shot manipulation

principles.title: Object-centric representation
principles.desc: Anchor manipulation understanding in object geometry and interaction — not absolute trajectories in camera space

principles.title: Geometric constraint extraction
principles.desc: Distill latent spatial constraints and structural priors from few demonstrations into reusable manipulation knowledge

principles.title: Zero-shot transfer
principles.desc: Generalize to novel objects, scenes, and embodiments without per-instance retraining

technology.demoDesc: From human-centric multimodal capture to cross-scene expansion and cross-embodiment retargeting — how one skill understanding transfers to new environments and robot platforms

demos.title: Human-centric multimodal teaching
demos.desc: Wearable sensing records vision, touch, and motion during manipulation — high-quality demos for generalization models

demos.title: One demo, a thousand scene variants
demos.desc: Object-centric representation expands a single demonstration across new poses, layouts, and lighting — no re-collection

demos.title: Tabletop skills on a bimanual humanoid
demos.desc: Pick-and-place on a Paxini humanoid shows the same skill transferring zero-shot across robot bodies

demos.title: Map human motion onto a humanoid
demos.desc: SparkUMR retargets everyday actions like drinking onto Fourier GR3 while preserving contact and posture

demos.title: Desktop organization, retargeted
demos.desc: Human motions for arranging a phone and laptop transfer to GR3 — fine manipulation that travels with the skill

demos.title: One kitchen skill, many robots
demos.desc: The same mixing and scooping routine drives different humanoid platforms — a unified skill model across embodiments
